title: Aspect for Real Estate and Construction: Organize Project Media
summary: One organized system for every site capture, walkthrough, and progress update so every stakeholder can find what they need.
body_markdown:
---


## The Problem


- Project media is stored by whoever captured it, with no connection to how the project is actually organized. Six months into a development, finding a specific phase capture means knowing which contractor shot it, what they named the file, and where they put it.
- A single development touches too many stakeholders with too many different access needs. Owners, GCs, subcontractors, architects, leasing agents, marketing agencies, and ownership groups all need different files at different levels of clearance.
- Version tracking matters over long timelines and is usually missing. Without a clear history of what was captured when and what was approved, milestone reporting turns into a reconstruction exercise.
- Downstream handoffs get rebuilt from scratch every time. Investor updates, sales enablement packages, leasing materials, and marketing assets all draw from the same project media, but most teams assemble them by hand each time instead of packaging from an organized source.


---


## What Aspect Does for Real Estate and Construction Teams


Aspect gives development teams the structure to keep media findable, shareable, and ready to package across the full lifecycle, without a coordinator managing it all by hand.


- Any team member finds the right site capture, walkthrough, or progress update in seconds, even without knowing who shot it, what it was named, or where it was filed
- Every stakeholder gets exactly the access they need from the same project record, with no manual export required
- Investor updates, leasing packages, and marketing handoffs pull from the approved source set instead of getting rebuilt before every milestone


---


## The Solution


### Custom Metadata and AI Search


Real estate and construction projects are organized by sites, phases, buildings, units, milestones, and handoff stages.


Custom metadata lets the library reflect how the project actually works. Every asset carries the fields that matter. A leasing agent looking for the approved exterior captures from phase two of a specific building searches by site and phase, not by folder. A project manager pulling together a milestone report filters by approval state and date range instead of asking the GC which drive the photos are on. Automated tagging applies those labels at ingest.


### Permissions and Guest Access


No other production environment deals with the same number of overlapping stakeholders as a real estate development. Permissions and guest access let every stakeholder operate from the same project record without seeing what they shouldn't. The ownership group sees the full development library.


For development teams onboarding new contractors and vendors regularly across long project timelines, this is what makes access management workable at scale.


Guest access brings outside reviewers into the review process without giving them full workspace exposure. A capital partner can review progress documentation for a quarterly investor update without seeing the active working files the construction team is using. An attorney can access the documentation relevant to a lease review without navigating the entire project library.
